reactions.author: rhdunn
reactions.text:
It's interesting how all the recent SOTA models are in the 1T-3T range. This even has a large number of active parameters (A52B). It is also likely that OpenAI, Anthropic, et. al. have similar sized models.

This has two effects: 1) it prevents effective use of these models on consumer-grade hardware; and 2) it pushes the requirements to train and run these models on existing and future data centres, making them more expensive to run.

It would be nice to have more slimmer models and more active research that isn't just "let's throw more compute at the problem". Maybe they'll train smaller models from the large model like Qwen have done in the past.
reactions.context: HN thread "We're releasing the weights of Mistral Large 4", top-level comment #5

reactions.author: maxloh
reactions.text:
> 2. If the Licensee or any of its affiliates operates a Model as a Service business, the Licensee must enter into a separate commercial license with Mistral before using the Model or its derivative works for any commercial purpose. The Licensee may contact Mistral, using this form: https://mistral.ai/contact/, to request a commercial license. [0]

reactions.author: kouteiheika
reactions.text:
These statistics and safeguards are pretty much meaningless, because it's completely trivial to get around them. You can prefill and edit the model's responses/thinking and force it to agree to virtually anything even with unmodified weights, and if you don't want to bother with jailbreaking and can host it yourself it's essentially a one-man weekend project to uncensor the model and have it agree with anything you want by default.

Guardrails on open-weight models is security theater purely to shield whoever released them from a potential PR nightmare.

reactions.author: kalenkilgore
reactions.text:
I understand your desire to have smaller models that are SOTA, but it may be more difficult than you realize. Think of it this way, a 100m model is like an infant, in fact we can make a table:

100m  = infant

1b    = toddler

100b  = age seven

1T    = teenager

10T   = 35 year old adult

And this tracks, because more compute allows the systems to parse more data, and learn over more cyber years. The reason that you cannot find a seven year old as smart as the average teenager is because intelligence NEEDS more data to learn more.

You can do hacks and tricks at the margins for marginal gains, but more compute for smarter models may just be a law of physics for how intelligence is made.

reactions.author: hintymad
reactions.text:
>  That's why we had huge backlash w

Training a frontier model is prohibitively expensive, so it’s understandable that open weights aren’t truly open source. In fact, I worry whether open weights will even survive[1] once the current AI cycle cools down. An even bigger issue is that as long as model development remains this capital intensive, a genuinely open-source community around frontier AI is virtually impossible. That will have massive implications for our careers. The more capital concentrates at the top, the less leverage we’ll have in the job market.

[1] Arguably hardware companies like Nvidia have incentives to subsidize open models to drive GPU demand. That said, I'm not sure how sustainable and sufficient that incentive can be.

reactions.author: berkes
reactions.text:
I've been using it since February this year almost exclusively. Occasionally ran the same prompt through openrouter to check if it's "my context" or "the model" when I get a poor result.

Mistrals models aren't the best. They certainly are measurably worse when I run them "blank slate". That is: without skills, AGENTS.md, MCPs and so on. But who does that anyway?

Aside from these harnesses, I run many one-off agent threads. They run at most half an hour and fill the context window not even 20% before I stop and "handover". And I tend to be annoyingly demanding and nitpicky in my skills, AGENT.md, prompts and issues (that an agent uses as prompt).

In my workflow, the context is what makes or breaks how well the task is performed almost all of the times. Mistrals models aren't "the best" - some Chinese models are cheaper (with similar outcome), and anthropics' models outperform the output consistently but for 20x or more of the price of Mistral (that is: when using the API/token pricing). But Mistrals models are certainly "good enough". Good enough is good, too.
